concept.name: Kubernetes
concept.title: Kubernetes, for Software Engineers
concept.definition: Kubernetes reconciles desired state with actual state: a Deployment owns a ReplicaSet, the ReplicaSet keeps Pods alive, the Scheduler places them on Nodes, and a Service routes traffic to them.
concept.problem: Engineers need repeatable deployment, recovery, placement, and stable networking across a changing pool of machines and processes.

goals: debug desired state versus actual state
identify the layer where a failure occurs

nodes.label: kubectl / CI
nodes.caption: declares desired state
nodes.description: kubectl, CI, and controllers create or update Kubernetes objects through the API Server.

nodes.label: Client
nodes.caption: application traffic
nodes.description: A browser, service, or test calling the workload through a Service rather than a Pod IP.

nodes.label: API Server
nodes.caption: control-plane front door
nodes.description: The API Server authenticates, validates, and stores Kubernetes objects. Every control-plane participant goes through it.

nodes.label: Service
nodes.caption: stable virtual IP
nodes.description: A Service selects matching Pods and provides a stable virtual address while Pod IPs change.

nodes.label: Deployment
nodes.caption: replicas + Pod template
nodes.description: A Deployment expresses the desired replica count and Pod template, and manages rollout through ReplicaSets.

nodes.label: Scheduler
nodes.caption: chooses a Node
nodes.description: The Scheduler watches for unbound Pods and selects a Node that satisfies resources and placement constraints.

nodes.label: ReplicaSet
nodes.caption: keeps N matching Pods
nodes.description: The ReplicaSet controller creates or deletes Pods until actual replicas match the desired count.

nodes.label: Pod A
nodes.caption: scheduled unit
nodes.description: A Pod is the unit the Scheduler binds to a Node and kubelet runs.

nodes.label: Pod B
nodes.caption: another replica
nodes.description: Another live replica owned by the same ReplicaSet and independently scheduled.

groups.label: Cluster
groups.description: Control-plane components plus the Nodes that run workloads.

groups.label: Control Plane
groups.description: The API-driven control loop that stores desired state and decides placement.

groups.label: Worker Node — kubelet runs the Pods
groups.description: One machine where kubelet starts and monitors the bound Pods.

chapters.title: Declare desired state
chapters.explanation: You submit a Deployment through the API Server. Its replica count and Pod template describe what should exist, not a one-time sequence of commands.
takeaways: API Server is the control-plane front door

chapters.title: ReplicaSet keeps Pods alive
chapters.explanation: The Deployment owns a ReplicaSet. The ReplicaSet controller creates and replaces Pods until the live count matches desired state.
takeaways: Deleting a Pod does not change desired replicas

chapters.title: Scheduler places Pods on Nodes
chapters.explanation: New Pods are unbound. The Scheduler selects a Node for each Pod; a Pending Pod often means resources or constraints prevent this step.

chapters.title: Reconcile actual state
chapters.explanation: Controllers repeatedly observe objects through the API Server and move actual state toward desired state. Kubernetes is a set of control loops, not a single deploy script.

chapters.title: Route clients to changing Pods
chapters.explanation: Clients call the Service. Its selector tracks matching Pods, keeping the client address stable across rescheduling and rollout.

roleRelevance.title: Why this matters for a software engineer
points: Debug from the object model: Deployment, ReplicaSet, Pod, Node, and Service.
Interpret Pending Pods as a scheduling, capacity, or placement-constraint signal.
Expect controllers to recreate deleted resources when desired state still requires them.
Use the API Server as the control-plane boundary for kubectl, CI, and automation.

contextCards.title: How the pieces fit
points: Deployment owns ReplicaSet; ReplicaSet owns Pods.
Service selects Pods independently of ownership.

contextCards.title: Useful debugging boundaries
points: Accepted spec but no Pod: inspect controllers and events.
Pending Pod: inspect requests, capacity, taints, and affinity.
Healthy Pod but no traffic: inspect Service selection and networking.

contextCards.title: Why this exists
points: Reconcile instead of scripting every recovery action.
Roll out and scale through desired state.
Decouple client addresses from ephemeral Pods.
